title: The Binance instances are Active with their deposit address recorded as TBD
content:
The Binance section stores "the Ethereum Mainnet Instances of Binance with `Active` Status" (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.1.14) and contains two: USDC to Binance receiving USDT, and USDT to Binance receiving USDC. Both are fully parameterised — token and underlying addresses, a 5,000,000 `maxAmount`, a 100,000,000 per day slope, a 0.2% `maxSlippage`, a `rechargeRate`. Both record `Binance Deposit Address`: "TBD" (.14.1.2.2.3, .14.2.2.2.3).

For a transfer-to-an-address conduit, that field is the conduit. As the Paxos instances demonstrate, the destination address is what selects the counterparty, the route and the asset to be received; every other parameter merely bounds an action that cannot be performed without it.

The placeholder here is also weaker than the Artifact's usual convention. Elsewhere unfinished values read "This parameter will be specified in a future iteration of the Spark Artifact" — a commitment with a named mechanism. "TBD" is a drafting note that has been published in a governance document as though it were a value.

The practical position is that these instances are inert: no address, no transfer, and under whitelist-by-rate-limit a route that cannot be executed is a route that is not authorised. The concern is presentational rather than operational — an `Active` label and a complete-looking parameter block on a conduit that is, in the one field that matters, undecided.
description: Both Binance conduits fully specify limits and slippage while the Binance Deposit Address — the only field that determines where the funds actually go — reads TBD.
